## VIC column closure: a mirror ghost folded into the end blocks (`Bnd`) {#sec-ch07-vic-closure}

### Summary

The system of @eq-ch07-vic-blocks reaches one cell beyond each end of the column. The VIC takes the increment
there to be the reflection of its neighbour's. That is a closed wall: no mass, transverse momentum or energy
crosses it, and the normal momentum keeps the wall pressure.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Closes each column's system at its ends and next to solids with a mirror ghost; @eq-ch07-vic-closure.

**Data.** Reads $\mathsf B_0$, $\mathsf C_{n_{\mathrm{lay}}-1}$ and the solid flags; writes the first and last diagonal blocks.

**Placement.** In the assembly, on the first and last rows of the column.

**Activation.** None; fixed by the kernel, whatever the boundary condition of the explicit stage.

**Guarantee / limits.** A reflecting closure in every case: mass, transverse momentum and energy do not cross it.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch07-vic-closure-tests; no dedicated ctest; `vic_closure_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C5]`.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}=\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,1,1,1)$ (or $\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,1)$) [-] is the wall parity of the solved
variables, `Bnd` in the code; $\mathsf J_0$ and $\mathsf J_{-1}$ are the flux Jacobians $\partial\mathbf F/\partial\mathbf U_{\mathrm{sv}}$ at
the first cell and at its mirror ghost, and $\mathsf J^{\mathrm{Roe}}$ the one at their Roe state (@sec-ch07-vic-assembly);
$\boldsymbol\delta_{-1}$, $\boldsymbol\delta_{n_{\mathrm{lay}}}$ are the ghost increments and $n_{\mathrm{lay}}$ the number of layers. The increments are in the
solved variables of @sec-ch07-vic-assembly, total-mass basis.

### Derivation

Setting $\boldsymbol\delta_{-1} = \mathsf P_{\mathrm w}\,\boldsymbol\delta_0$ in the first row and
$\boldsymbol\delta_{n_{\mathrm{lay}}} = \mathsf P_{\mathrm w}\,\boldsymbol\delta_{n_{\mathrm{lay}}-1}$ in the last gives

$$
\mathsf A_0 \leftarrow \mathsf A_0 + \mathsf B_0\,\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}, \quad \mathsf A_{n_{\mathrm{lay}}-1} \leftarrow \mathsf A_{n_{\mathrm{lay}}-1} + \mathsf C_{n_{\mathrm{lay}}-1}\,\mathsf P_{\mathrm w} .
$$ {#eq-ch07-vic-closure}

Row 0 is $\mathsf B_0\boldsymbol\delta_{-1}+\mathsf A_0\boldsymbol\delta_0+\mathsf C_0\boldsymbol\delta_1=\mathbf f_0$; with
$\boldsymbol\delta_{-1}=\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}\boldsymbol\delta_0$ it becomes
$(\mathsf A_0+\mathsf B_0\mathsf P_{\mathrm w})\boldsymbol\delta_0+\mathsf C_0\boldsymbol\delta_1=\mathbf f_0$, and the last row likewise with
$\mathsf C_{n_{\mathrm{lay}}-1}$. This equals solving with the ghosts kept and eliminated, within the $10^{-12}$ relative threshold (`[C1]`).
Without the closure the column loses mass through its ends (`[C3]`).

Why the wall carries no mass, transverse momentum or energy:

1. The Euler flux is odd under the mirror: $\mathbf F(\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}\mathbf U)=-\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}\mathbf F(\mathbf U)$.
   Differentiating, $\mathsf J_{-1}\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}=-\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}\mathsf J_0$ for a ghost that mirrors the first cell.
2. The Roe state of a mirrored pair has zero normal velocity (`[C4]`). There the eigenvalues are $-c_s$, 0 and $+c_s$,
   so $\mathsf A^-=\mathsf R\lvert\Lambda\rvert\mathsf R^{-1}=(\mathsf J^{\mathrm{Roe}})^2/c_s$, since $\lvert\lambda\rvert=\lambda^2/c_s$ for each of
   them. At zero normal velocity $\mathsf J^{\mathrm{Roe}}$ anticommutes with $\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}$ (step 1 with the two states
   equal), so its square, and $\mathsf A^-$, commute with $\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}$.
3. The linearised face flux is $\tfrac12(\mathsf J_{-1}\boldsymbol\delta_{-1}+\mathsf J_0\boldsymbol\delta_0)-\tfrac12\mathsf A^-(\boldsymbol\delta_0-\boldsymbol\delta_{-1})$.
   With $\boldsymbol\delta_{-1}=\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}\boldsymbol\delta_0$ and step 1 it is
   $\tfrac12(\mathsf I-\mathsf P_{\mathrm w})\mathsf J_0\boldsymbol\delta_0-\tfrac12(\mathsf I-\mathsf P_{\mathrm w})\mathsf A^-\boldsymbol\delta_0$ by step 2. The
   factor $\mathsf I-\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}$ is zero in every row with $\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}=+1$, so those rows of the wall flux
   vanish (`[C5]`, for $N=3$ and 5).
4. On a moving, layered Cartesian column, the column sums of the mass, transverse momentum and energy rows of the
   closed operator vanish within the $10^{-13}$ check threshold. The normal momentum row keeps an order-one wall term, the wall
   pressure (`[C2]`).
5. *Round-off.* $\mathsf B_0\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}$ only flips the sign of a column, which is exact; adding it to $\mathsf A_0$
   rounds each entry once, within $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2$ of $|\mathsf A_0|+|\mathsf B_0|$ entrywise.

In the code, @eq-ch07-vic-closure is the closure with `Bnd` ({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch07-vic-closure for the bottom end.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch07-vic-closure
#| fig-cap: "The bottom of a column. The ghost increment (purple, dashed) is the mirror $\\mathsf P_{\\mathrm w}\\,\\boldsymbol\\delta_0$ of the first cell's, $\\mathsf P_{\\mathrm w}=\\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,1,1,1)$, so its coupling $\\mathsf B_0\\boldsymbol\\delta_{-1}$ folds into the diagonal block as in @eq-ch07-vic-closure. The top is the same with $\\mathsf C_{n_{\\mathrm{lay}}-1}$."
#| fig-alt: "A dashed purple ghost cell left of a thick wall line and two interior cells to its right, with an arrow from the first cell to the ghost and the closure formula beside them."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch07.figures.fig_vic_closure import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The full kernel sets `Bnd` with $-1$ on the normal momentum ({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}). It
adds the closure at the first and last cell of the column and next to a solid cell, unless the block is not the
first or last in $x_1$ or the direction is periodic. The dispatch always passes `periodic` as false
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}). The partial kernel does the same with its $3\times3$ `Bnd`
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_partial_impl.h vic_assemble_partial_impl >}}). Its $m_a$ fold (@eq-ch07-vic-fold) treats the
tangential momenta the way $\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}$ does, with parity $+1$: a face merged into the end block, `merged_lower` or
`merged_upper`, adds its $m_a$ columns to the end block's and takes the end cell's $v_a$ and $\tilde m_a$
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_partial_impl.h vic_assemble_partial_impl >}}). The blocks next to a solid cell use a mirror of the fluid
cell instead of the solid's state, so the solid acts as a wall from inside the column, through `solid_lower`
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}).

: Code map of the VIC column closure. {#tbl-ch07-vic-closure-code}

**How to use it.** There is no key, and the closure ignores the YAML boundary condition of $x_1$: an open or outflow
explicit boundary still gets a reflecting implicit wall (Limits 1). @eq-ch07-vic-closure is these lines
({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}}):

```cpp
  Bnd.setConstant(1.);
  Bnd(IVX + dir) = -1;
  ...
  if ((i == is || solid_lower) && first_block && !periodic)
    a[i] += b[i] * Bnd.asDiagonal();
  if ((i == ie || solid_upper) && last_block && !periodic)
    a[i] += c[i] * Bnd.asDiagonal();
```

`Bnd.asDiagonal()` is $\mathsf P_{\mathrm w}$, with $-1$ on the normal momentum `IVX + dir`; the two updates are the bottom
and top halves of @eq-ch07-vic-closure, also applied next to a solid cell. Refused: nothing.

: Tests of the VIC column closure. {#tbl-ch07-vic-closure-tests}

No ctest checks the closure on its own, so its own tolerance is missing evidence. `vic_closure_check.py` ports the
closure with zero gravity on an 8-layer moving column with mirror ghosts.[^ch07-vic-closure-run] `[C1]` matches the
explicit-ghost solve within $10^{-12}$ relative; `[C2]` gives column sums below $10^{-13}$ for mass,
transverse momentum and energy and above $10^{-3}$ for the normal momentum; `[C3]` loses $1.24\times10^{-2}$ of the mass without
the closure; `[C4]` gives a Roe normal velocity of 0 at both walls; `[C5]` checks steps 1 to 3 exactly. CPU and CUDA
share the headers; only the CPU path ran.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The implicit closure is always a reflecting wall. A column whose explicit boundary is open, or an outflow,
still has a closed wall in its implicit solve.
:::

1. **Mismatch with the explicit boundary.** The assembled end blocks use the ghost states the explicit boundary
   condition filled. Only for a reflecting boundary are those the mirror the closure assumes.
2. **No periodic $x_1$.** The periodic branch is unreachable, since the dispatch passes false.
3. **No dedicated test.** No ctest checks the closure on its own.
